First off, the product looks and sounds great. The first time I picked it up, I figured it would be a five star product. But then came the smell and fumes.
I noticed the smell initially but figured it would dissipate quickly. I was wrong. The smell of paint or lacquer--something like that--is so strong that the smell lingers in a room long after the product is removed. Being in a room with that product is enough to get a strong dose. I was lightheaded within 5 minutes and the feeling stayed for a good hour. The headache that accompanied it lingered for far longer.
So I tried to correct the problem. I hung out up in the garage with a fan locked on high one foot in front of it, and I left it like that all weekend. The garage was pungent until Wednesday. But that did eventually fade. However, now, if I so much as blow on the product once, even though the sound is AMAZING, the lightheaded feeling returns. So as a whistle, it is useless to me. I can't even display it anywhere besides my garage without the room itself carrying the smell and inducing a headache and lightheadedness.
I would recommend the product if it didn't make me physically sick, but I can't. I deeply regret this purchase.
The product was crafted very skillfully and for this reason alone I give it two stars instead of one. I still recommend against buying it though.

I ordered 3 rings from this seller, Core Carbon Rings, including this one. All 3 looked and felt great. The only issue was that I ordered 1/2 a size too big. After sending a message to the seller, I received lightning fast responses for all subsequent messages too.

I ordered the twill matte, twill glossy, and legacy gloss rings. They all look spectacular, but I decided I liked the twill glossy best.

The matte twill ring is a little gray in comparison to the glossy rings since there is no varnish layer, but that layer can be scratched. So I liked the matte ring for its scratch resistance.

The glossy twill is blacker (due to the epoxy layer on top) than the matte version and the carbon fiber pattern looks more 3D and has more depth in my opinion. it also matches colors better with my carbon fiber pitaka watch band. The possibility of scratches is something I’m willing to risk for a great looking design.

The glossy legacy ring was my favorite design. I like how the cf weave is different than the traditional weave. It was a hard decision choosing between this and the glossy twill, but I decided that the twill weave stood out more and the legacy is more subtle, plus my wife liked the glossy twill the best.

I hope my review helps others when deciding on a cf ring. I do not hesitate to give all of them my highest recommendation.

I will start off by saying I love this hair, but...

A bit of back story: I have short real thin messy dreads (12 in) and have had dread extensions added to my hair for over 15 years. I haven't had real hair (that stuff that normal people brush daily) in over 20 years, so this review is based on my knowledge and experience in comparison to my use of normal dread extensions. I also want to point out that I love daddydread dreads and use his dreads exclusively. Here is my review of the Curly dreadlocks:

Pluses:

+ Light weight. I weigh 3 lbs less with these than I do with regular dread extensions. That's 3 lbs less weight on my neck

+ They are so soft. They feel so nice against my skin.

+ They are beautiful. I love the curls so much.

Minuses:

- coverage vs. cost. I normally order 80 dreads from the same dread maker and that is normally far more than enough to fully cover my head and have some extras to add later, but 80 of these didn't even cover 1/2 of my head. (Mind you I have a thin mohawk with the sides shaved- so to not get 1/2 coverage with 80 dreads means these are very thin). But, keep in mind, 80 of these dreads are the same cost as 80 regular dreads. So you would have to pay more than double for the same coverage, and they aren't cheap.

-Fray and friz and general upkeep. These friz so easily. In order to keep them from frizzing I would spray them every day with a water solution with a tiny amount of fabric softener and brush wet only. These also fray so much quicker and I ended up cutting the fray out often. These had to be treated like a wig much more than treated like dread extensions, which we all know require work.

Ultimately my personal opinion is that at the current price I would only do this hair again for short term wear for a very special occasion that warranted the additional cost (i.e. wedding, or very special vacation). If the price dropped to 1/2 price I would consider these for daily use, even though they are more of a hassle they are prettier so it would be worth the hassle at a lower price point, but I just can't afford to use these daily since the coverage is so thin and the price so high. I honestly think to get a good full heads worth of coverage you would easily need to spend over $500.

I've purchased several of these cute little pillows over the past year or so. I don't do a lot of decorating for holidays throughout the year, but I do like to put out a little something to acknowledge what time of year it is.

These pillows are perfect for just that--acknowledging what time of year it is without going overboard. I have a small easel I stand the pillow in. It sits on a narrow mantel shelf in my kitchen along with other décor, flowers, framed family pics, etc. which I'm always changing.

I ordered a state pillow for our state holiday--love the retro design! So I ordered other state pillows. Whenever we have guests from out-of-state I like to put out their state pillow--they love it! I've even sent them home with a state pillow from our state, as a souvenir of their visit. Of course, I included an easel, too!

I'm able to store all the pillows I've ordered thus far in a single shoe box, which is one reason I enjoy these--they take up very little storage space, which is important in our small home! They don't break if dropped or knocked over. And they're not overly expensive.

So yes, keep in mind these pillows are very small. One pillow would easily get lost on a sofa or chair. It might work on a bed, with larger throw pillows behind it. And you mustn't get them wet--just dust them off. (I've never had a problem with that, thankfully!) But these have proven to be perfect for my needs and for that reason I'm happy to give this product five stars. I look forward to purchasing more.

The entire point of something like this is to "motivate" kids by having their score posted publicly. This is the definition of shame. It reduces children to their behavior and is even more problematic with the early childhood years (7 and under) because their behavior is even less in their control and more based on other factors.

It is entirely possible to correct behavior and address issues without posting an arbitrary behavior score to the entire class. Even for the children who seem to be happy with these charts and do well with them can become preocupied with their score and form opinions on their classmates based on the chart and not their actual experiences with them.
The same goes for behavior based charts at home. Even without a classroom of kids, your child gets the message that mom likes them when they are good and doesn't when they don't do the right thing. They get preoccupied with the chart and performing for the parent and don't truly internalize the "why" behind what the chart is trying to get them to do. You don't need to be in public to feel shamed. Even without intentionally shaming it happens.

This type of chart was used in a work place with ADULTS during training, and it turns out that adults absolutely hate this public display of behavior. It resulted in anxiety, disengagement, fear, resentment, and embarrassment. If adults don't like these tools, how do you think kids feel?

We all do the best we know at the time, and life is a continual learning process. There are 100% better ways to teach and parent than this and intrinsically motivate kids.

(A visual routine chart where kids know what is coming next is something else entirely and those are very helpful.)

Reasons I bought this press:
1.) Rolling tortillas takes a lot of time and effort for what I get out of it. My husband LOVES the homemade tortillas, I personally am fine with store bought. So making homemade wasn't something I did very often. I wanted a press that would make the process less effort for me. This press overall does make the process easier. It does not make the tortillas as thin as I would like on its own. I use a cut gallon bag ziplock bag as a liner so after I press them I also roll them. The press does give me a good, round starting point so that I only have to roll a couple of times before I get the thickness I want.

2.) I wanted to be able to make large tortillas/pizza dough. This was the reason I chose THIS press. Most of the presses aren't as big as this one. I do like that I can make a large pizza crust quickly without having to roll out sticky dough. Our family easily eats 2 pizza's in one meal and will only need to make more as our boys get older. This press will be a life saver over the years.

3.) This press is beautiful. I can leave it on the counter and use it frequently without having to dig out another piece of kitchen equipment. I don't use/have a lot of specialty kitchen equipment, but this was one thing I requested.

The reason it gets 4 stars is that it doesn't get the flour tortilla's as thin as I would like. To be fair I knew it would be a long shot to get something to press the tortillas super thin, but I expected this press to get them thinner after reading other reviews. I added extra layers (super thin cutting boards) to help make the tortillas thinner, but even that was insufficient.

Overall, I would recommend this press. It feels like it will last for years to come and I look forward to making many delicious tortillas/pizzas/???.

This is an August Derleth Elder Sign, not HP Lovecraft.  Mr. Derleth didn't know that HP Lovecraft had described what an Elder Sign looked like in his correspondence with other writers, so he made up his own interpretation.  Lin Carter later tried to reconcile the two in his own writings by putting the HP Lovecraft Elder Sign inside the Derleth Elder Sign, and writing that he wasn't sure which part of the sign held the power.  All that said, the August Derleth sign is the pop-culture aware version of the Elder Sign.  Only us purists know it isn't the real one!

This arrives well packaged in a fold-top acetate bag.
If giving as a gift, this is challenging to wrap as it arrives. I suggest finding an appropriately sized box to wrap it in or use a standard sized gift bag. This is a nice *almost* standalone any occasion gift for any purse using gal or murse using guy as it is neither overtly feminine nor masculine. The reason I say '*almost* standalone gift' is that I was raised to never gift a purse &/or wallet without including 2 cents or more (I usually include a dollar) - I think (if I remember right) this is a superstition that giving an empty purse/wallet is wishing the recipient to always be broke & including some kind of money is wishing the recipient financial abundance. Do with that what you will.
I loved the note tucked inside the purse from the crafter. While it was printed/typed, it had the heartfelt wording of a handwritten note & was very nice.
The workmanship is wonderful. No loose seams/threads, obvious attention to detail, quality construction. You can tell the crafter cares about & enjoys their craft!
It has a wonderful coloration & smells great (I love the smell of leather)! While the included note suggests that using the purse will give it a patina & dissipate the smell, I've always used a quality (& time tested company) leather protectant & this is no exception. I like the coloration that it currently is & want to keep it this way. The 'leather smell' WILL dissipate with time no matter what.
The outside back of this purse has a medium-small zippered pocket & the front has a large (mainly open) pocket. Though this pocket does have a snap-tab, it doesn't do much in the way of securing items. I find this to be a great place to store my phone, a pen or 2, & other items of that nature that I want to quickly access frequently.
Inside, there is an open pocket on each side, approximately the same size as the tabbed pocket outside. On one of these pockets is a section to hold 2 cards such as ID/credit or debit card/ membership/loyalty &/or business cards. I use this to hold my most frequently accessed membership/loyalty cards that don't have a keychain tab option. The main area inside is sizable, able to hold a Kindle Fire & a full sized wallet (the kind that allows your bills to lie flat rather than having to fold them), amongst other things.
I consider this a medium sized purse (coming from an 'It girl' purse) which still allows me to carry all my day-to-day needs & wants.
I highly recommend!

I have to say that I bought it to honor my beloved fur baby, who I lost a year ago. I was looking for a frame that had this sentiment, but didn't like the ones I saw. I also have to say that I removed the charm (the "You left paw prints on my Heart" charm) from the band, and attached it to a picture frame of my fur baby. It's perfect there, and my Fitbit is still perfect without the charm. Even better, as I found the charm slightly annoying that it would hit the metal and make a lot of noise, and hit my arm/wrist and irritate me. But, that's just me, probably because I have Fibromyalgia and I'm more sensitive. I wore it for weeks before I took it off and it was annoying to me, but fine; like a charm bracelet.

Also, the FitBit works perfectly with the band, and keeps track of everything I need it to. I don't have to worry about it falling off (like with another band I had) as the lock is very tight, to the point of almost being difficult to take off. But better that than to be so loose you lose it.

All in all, I LOVE this band, and I highly recommend it.

The only thing is that they aren't really prints. They are photographs. As such, the 8"X10" (the size I bought) are exactly that size. There is no white/blank area around the image. The image goes right to the edges, just like a photograph. They are also printed on photo paper (or paper very similar to photo paper) and look just like photos. Usually, when you buy a print, there is a blank area "framing" the image. It may be very thin, but it is there. Also, usually photographs are not considered prints.

The lack of any blank area around the image, made these VERY difficult to matte and frame. If you had it done professionally, it would be fine, but part of the image would be lost. I purchased frames with mattes here on Amazon, though, and the mattes were cut exactly 8"X10". This made it difficult to mount these photos/prints in as they were the exact same size as the opening. There wasn't even a tiny bit of overlap. I had to tape them in very carefully and place a dark piece of paper behind them so that if there was a small slit between the edge of the print/photo and the edge of the matte, it would be a uniform dark color. In the end they look just fine. It just isn't what one expects when one buys a "print." So, if you are thinking of purchasing these prints/photos, keep this in mind when deciding on how to frame or hang them.

I have only recently discovered archery, specifically instinctive shooting--and cursed my foolishness for not discovering it earlier. Like all new enthusiasts to the sport, I went a little overboard and ended up buying not one but three bows: a Primal Gear folding bow, a mongolian-style recurve, and this one, a beautifully light & balanced hickory longbow. As any longbow shooter can tell you, it takes time and practice to achieve any kind of real proficiency, so believe me, I've been putting in some time and practice. Since I'm new to the sport, I don't have a lot of grounds for comparison, but I know good craftsmanship when I see it, when I hold it in my hands.
I love this bow. I know without doubt when I'm shooting badly the fault is mine, on me, not this marvelous piece of work.

Since I've found such joy in archery, I felt like sharing and bought a bow each for my daughter and son-in-law. For my daughter, I bought a beautiful but simply designed recurve modeled after the traditional Chinese style. I bought one of these longbows for my son-in-law, thinking he would have an affinity for its elegant simplicity, as I do.

Anyway, if it isn't glaringly obvious, I strongly recommend buying this longbow. You'll have to keep it oiled to protect the wood, to keep it pliable and more weather-resistant. I use lemon oil since it works so well on my rifle stocks. There are other wood oils, of course.

John Rocque, a map-maker who lived in London in the 1700s, completed a masterful plan of the city measuring about 7' x 11', in 24 panels. This required ten years' work.

Scrolling ahead to the present, Old Maps has produced a detailed reprint of Rocque's original map for the enjoyment of travelers everywhere. The reprint job is finely done and includes the choice of several sizes that are reductions from the original, making them manageable for the home as opposed to the exhibition hall. Besides large landmarks I can see smaller ones such as The Church of All Hallows by the Tower. There is everything to like about the job that Old Maps has done, and nothing to dislike. I commend them for their work.

As for me, I'm someone who enjoys visiting London. Once this map is framed, I'll get to enjoy it vicariously. This will add to the pleasure of visiting the city someday in future.

I have found the dark etches of the charm seem to be lighter than they appear the photos (both those of the seller and my own which I took on my cellphone).
I would say the colour of the pencil lead (in my image) and the "darker," negative space appear to be almost the same tone in reality.

I'm rating this with 4 stars because leather tears, and three stress points look flimsy. See photo 4.
This is roomy, and holds a bunch of stuff. Since I enjoy writing, my every day carry includes B5 notepads by Tsubane, fountain pen sleeves, small pen bag, a few art pens. This is one of my better bags for everyday carry.
Cons:
There are a few things that are destined to break, zippers, D-ring stress points, carrying handle flap reinforcement, bottom/base padding.

Carrying strap is configured so the buckle is centered where it rests on my shoulder. There is a strap sleeve but it slides off the buckle
Also main strap D-ring connection on the bag isn't reinforced, and could easily tear. Of course strap is double stitched at D-rings on each edge, though strap is only single thickness that connects bag and strap. One is pulling away all ready.
Top carrying handle stress is on one layer of leather and I foresee tearing over time.

Pros:
Roomy, spacious, small pockets inside and out for documents. Front and side pockets are flexible enough to hold a lot of small items.
Seam stitching looks solid, time will only prove longevity. So far it's holding up okay without showing stray threads.
Some reviews have complained about smell; mine had a little, so I let it air out a few days before using it, and it seems to have worked. No glue smell though.
Leather is decently tanned and dyed, and a warning is enclosed to be aware dye could rub off on light colors. This can be alleviated with leather polish or cleaner.
CONCLUSION:
Overall this is a good bag for my use. I do believe the strap will tear without much provocation at D-ring stress points with what I carry.
Big question, will I buy from this supplier again? Probably, but I'll make sure stress points are stronger. I may gift this to someone and keep looking.
I do like this bag, one of my better choices and I'm keeping it. But I am taking it to a leather shop to have nylon zippers replaced with heavier duty metal and strap reinforced at stress points.
Inside bottom I'll add a a bottom stiff leather lining and I might have a bottom leather pad stitched outside bottom to protect it from tearing or getting caught on sharp objects. I commute so a little extra bottom padding won't create a problem. I'll also add reinforcement on inside flap handle. With these additions, this will be a great bag.

For reference, I had a camera bag strap rip at a D-ring and almost lost it while taking a picture. I also had a messenger bag strap rip at D-ring.
Photos:
Photo 1; everyday carry contents. Writing pads, ink cartridges, fountain pen cases, blue pen case holds art pens and pencils, earbuds. End pocket is high power flashlight; plus a packet for personal things.

When I tested it, I added my 12inch MacBook Pro and iPad, dongles and cords in addition to items in photo1. They fit comfortably inside, though it was too much weight for this, so I carry those in a different bag.
With stronger support on bottom, side ring strap and top handle, This bag will last a long time.

[[VIDEOID:4a532d2f8f144f3a079692661a2d437b]] I developed a terrible habit of picking the heels of my feet, and have been looking for ages for a fidget that would help me stop. Nothing has worked as well as this! I hadn't heard of picking stones before seeing this. There's a lot of imitation ones out there, but this is the original. I can't say how the others compare.

What I like:

* The filler is great for fulfilling that need to actually pick and pull something off of something. It's somewhat thick and is stretchy, but not excessively.

* As someone who also tends to excessively tweeze, I love that they give you a pair of needle nose tweezers to pick at the filler. It also has a dentist pick, which is great for getting pieces out of the hard to reach places. They're both satisfying to use.

* I love the use of sequins on the second stone! If you have a bad habit of picking scabs, this is a very similar sensation. I did pick those off over the box so that I could reuse them, but wasn't as successful at adding them on as they were originally done.

* The filler is very satisfying to pick with just your nails as well. It's what I personally prefer, but I do use the tools too.

What I don't like:

* It is messy. I don't think there's really any avoiding this and getting the same kind of satisfaction though. I recommend using the box to kind of catch the pieces.

* The filler takes overnight to dry. It's again probably something unavoidable and I refilled them before going to bed, but I wish there was a way to accelerate the drying.

* The lava rocks are very abrasive and easy to break off little bits. Definitely be careful if you're picking the filler with your fingernails because it can start to chaff your fingers.

* Now comes my #1 complaint: the refill for the filler that they sell on their site is too expensive to be accessible to most if you use this a lot. I easily used up the bottle included in the matter of a couple of days. I found myself not using it when I wanted to because I didn't want to go through it all after seeing that a 2oz bottle is $15.

If you plan to only use this occasionally, you wouldn't have to refill as frequently, but if you're using it like I am to try to deter yourself from skin picking, I'd personally probably need 3-4 bottles a week, if not more. That's $45 - $60 a week, and $180 - $240 per month for 24oz - 32oz of the filler. I'm going to try using cosmetic liquid latex instead because it's significantly cheaper. I may also try adding white glue to it to thicken it and see how it does.

Overall great concept and I really enjoyed the brief amount of time I was able to use these before running out of the filler, but I am sad that I can't get the same filler for an amount I could afford. I was hoping there'd be at least a larger bottle for cheaper per oz but only the 2oz bottle is offered.

Soap-making tradition on the large family farm was an institution ... mom, g-g-ma, g-ma, g-g aunts & uncles, aunts and uncles, dozens of cousins. It was a late-fall, early winter tradition, as I recall, shortly after the outdoor open fire, copper vat (we kids figured you could boil one of us in them), sales quantity, apple butter endlessly stirred by the cousins.

So I'm maybe ten years old and beginning my hired-hand, unpaid farm apprentice-ship. My recollection of homemade soap's main ingredients includes strange, clear slabs of jelly-like rendered hog fat, sacks of lye (bad stuff), and charcoal, among other things likely 200, maybe 300 years old. From these bases came a line of products. Pine tar soap for work hands, lye soap bars for dishes and laundry, and various soaps and cleansers made from dilution of the lye soap. The only soaps purchased included Ivory, Murphy's oil soap, and PineSol.

Yes, the lye soap could sting. We kids just thought the sting was what clean felt like.

The wall stencil has a very interesting pattern which has a modern look to it. If you are creative, you can create your own design within the over-all pattern. I used it for a small area no larger than the actual stencil size. On this scale, you can mix as few or as many colors as you like. For entire wall, stencil overlapping projects, it's best to keep to a single color.

For my project, I used acrylic paints and small brushes. This is not typical. The reason rollers are used by default is because the roller will press down over the stencil as you paint, thus keeping it in place. If you use brushes instead you'll have to press down along the corners of each area as you paint to prevent the paint from going beneath the stencil. The stencil does not come with any adhesive. You'll have to apply non-stick painters tape or similar spray glue to keep the stencil in its basic position.

The bracelet is adjusted by pulling the two drawstrings. I would recommend measuring the circumference of your wrist if you have smaller wrists. I have a 7.5" wrist and the bracelet is close to the limits of its adjustment, so the 7" size on the product page is accurate. The drawstrings have a small hematite bead at the end and they do hang down after the bracelet is adjusted. You can tuck them under the beaded part of the bracelet.

The necklace is simple and not heavy. The string is made of a light nylon cord, similar to but not as tough as paracord. The necklace has collar that can be moved up and down to tighten the cord that goes around your neck.

Both the bracelet and the necklace are well made and the synthetic threads used to make them are fused at the ends to prevent fraying. There was one tiny loose spot in the bracelet's thread at the beginning of the bead section, but the beads were not loose and it didn't affect function.

Review is of: "Jade Beads Bracelet, Green Jade and Sterling Silver Beads Bracelet, Nephrite Jade Bracelet"
——— LIKES: The jade and the beads look very nice together. The combo of silver and gold goes great with the green. The shine of the beads contrasted with the darker beads is pleasing.
— The jade is dark, mixed with black. The beads (6mm) are polished but not highly polished; this gives them a not-quite-matte look compared to the shiny metal. Again, another nice touch.
——— DISLIKES: The bracelet is slightly larger around than most others I have; it's about 7.25 instead of just 7.0 inches. Not a big deal, but it's slightly loose and therefore the beads move around more than I'd like. It would be nice if the bracelet was tighter (it is stretchy so that wouldn't have hurt) so it holds the beads more stationary.
— It looks good standalone or with other bracelets. It goes especially well with black or brown, I have a couple of leather ones it goes great with.
——— SUMMARY:
— A nicely made, aesthetically pleasing bracelet. The beads give it an Asian feel, besides it being jade. A very nice accessory. It makes me want to check out Kartini Studio's other offerings.
